theater: 長江下游建業石頭城（江蘇南京）

battle.name: 晉滅吳之戰
battle.theater: 長江下游建業石頭城（江蘇南京）
battle.brief: 咸寧四年冬，晉武帝發六路大軍二十餘萬自北南征，王濬造連舫大船自成都順流東下，杜預自荊州沿江策應，兵鋒直抵建業石頭城，孫皓出降，六十餘年分裂終結。吳軍沿岸以弩封鎖水道，晉舟師以蒙衝硬撼、弩手掩護登岸，江上互射自峽至吳門，歷四個月而吳亡。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 晉滅吳之戰是西晉咸寧四年（279）冬至太康元年（280）三月，晉武帝司馬炎動員六路大軍二十餘萬，對東吳孫皓政權發動的滅國戰爭。晉方的調度集中在中樞：以益州刺史王濬為龍驤將軍，統蜀中降附之眾與益州工匠所造的連舫大船，自成都沿江東下，經三峽直趨建業；以征南將軍杜預鎮荊州，率荊州軍自江陵順流而東；以鎮南將軍陶侃都督江州諸軍，自武昌沿江而下；以征虜將軍王渾自河南率步騎南征，進圖項城；平東將軍司馬伷以琅邪王鎮下邳，率眾循淮泗而下；另以安平王劉統為監軍，後方由許昌、洛陽轉輸糧械。吳方以建業為中樞，孫皓居中，倚大將張悌為長城，沿江自江陵、蘆洲、皖口至牛渚層層設防，江面布列舟師，岸上列弩手，水陸互為表裡。吳廷內部分為主戰與主降兩派，孫皓在請和與死戰之間遲疑不決，荊州與益州一線的守將各懷觀望，兵力號稱帶甲數十萬，卻分散在千餘里江防上，調度遲滯而士氣低落。
countriesEn: The conquest of Wu was the campaign in which Western Jin, from the last months of Xianning 4 (279) to the third month of Taikang 1 (280), mobilised six columns totalling more than two hundred thousand men against the regime of Sun Hao in Eastern Wu. On the Jin side the effort was directed from the centre. Wang Jun, Governor of Yizhou and appointed Dragon General, held the surrendered troops of Shu together with the connected-deck vessels built by the craftsmen of Yizhou, and launched from Chengdu down the river, through the Three Gorges and straight for Jianye. Du Yu, who had taken the title of Commander Southward, held Jingzhou and marched east from Jiangling down the water. Tao Kan, Commander Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of the Jiang region, came down from Wuchang along the bank. Wang Hun, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, led infantry and cavalry south out of Henan and turned his attention on the fortified town of Xiang. Sima Zhou, General of the Pacifying East and Prince of Langya, held Xiapi and moved down through the Huai and Si waters. Anping Prince Liu Tong served as supervisor of the operation, while the rear was fed and equipped from Xuchang and Luoyang. The Wu side centred on Jianye: Sun Hao sat in the middle of it and relied on the Great General Zhang Ti as the bulwark of the state, stringing defences along the river from Jiangling, Luzhou and Wankou down to Niuzhu, with fleets on the water and crossbowmen on the bank, land and river forming each other's cover. Inside the court the ministers split between war and surrender, Sun Hao hesitated between the two, and the commanders on the Jingzhou and Yizhou lines watched and waited. Wu's troops were numbered in tens of thousands on paper, but they were spread over a thousand li of river front, slow to move and low in spirit.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩朝。晉武帝司馬炎是發動戰爭並決定受降條件的人：咸寧四年十一月下詔發兵，他起初聽從眾議而猶豫，終因杜預力主速戰、王濬在蜀造舟成功而下定決心；孫皓遣使請降時，晉廷堅持受降必須以臣服為前提，孫皓反覆遷延，錯失機會。杜預是全戰役的戰略核心，他上表指出「今兵威已振，蜀民疲於供役，若不速戰，歲月既深，吳人習於戰，國怨民疲，勢必隳墜」，並承接前任羊祜先定蜀、後圖吳的次序；羊祜在荊州以屯田積穀、修農養兵、撫恤新附百姓換來人心，於太康元年之前病逝，未能見功，臨終上疏薦杜預自代。杜預率荊州軍破吳將張悌所部於板渚一線，又以小船載火炬夜渡江面，焚毀橫江浮橋，打通航道。張悌是吳廷最後能獨當一面的大將，其死使吳軍再無統一指揮。王濬是舟師的樞紐，他經營益州數年，徵召蜀匠造出方百二十步、可載二千餘人的連舫大船，領兵自成都東下，經牛渚、三山直抵石頭城下，迫使孫皓出降。陶侃自郢州一路沿江掃清吳軍水寨，王渾在項城牽制吳方西援，司馬伷在淮泗一線策應，三路與主力互相呼應。孫皓是敗亡一方的主角，其即位後的暴虐與無度供役正是士氣崩潰的根源；出降後封烏程侯，送居洛陽，四年後而卒。
peopleEn: The decisive figures belonged to the two courts. Sima Yan, Emperor Wu of Jin, was the man who set the war in motion and who fixed the terms of any surrender. He issued the edict in the eleventh month of Xianning 4 and was at first hesitant in the face of the court's opinion, making up his mind only after Du Yu argued for immediate war and Wang Jun's shipbuilding in Shu showed the thing could be done. When Sun Hao sent an envoy to ask for terms, the Jin court held that submission had to be unqualified, and Sun Hao's endless procrastination threw the chance away. Du Yu was the strategic core of the whole affair. His memorial set out the reasoning that the soldiery were now strong, that the people of Shu were exhausted by their labours, that if the war were not fought quickly the years would deepen, the people of Wu would grow used to war, the resentment of the country and the weariness of the people would make the structure collapse, and that only then could the attack be launched; the sequence of first settling Shu and only then turning on Wu had been laid down by his predecessor Yang Hu, who had governed Jingzhou by patient husbandry, storing grain, resting the army and sparing the new subjects. Yang Hu died before the victory was won, leaving a memorial recommending Du Yu as his successor. Du Yu's men beat the force of the Wu general Zhang Ti on the line of Ban Chu, and then put torches into small boats, ferrying them across by night to burn the floating barrier that lay across the channel, opening a passage. Zhang Ti was the last Wu general able to hold a sector alone, and with his death the Wu army had no single command any more. Wang Jun was the pivot of the flotilla: he had governed Yizhou for years, gathered the craftsmen of Shu to build connected-deck vessels a hundred and twenty paces across the beam that carried more than two thousand men apiece, led them down from Chengdu, passed Niuzhu and Sanshan and came to the foot of Stone City, forcing Sun Hao to surrender. Tao Kan swept the Wu river camps on the stretch between Wuchang and Jiangling, Wang Hun pinned the western relief at Xiang, and Sima Zhou supported from the Huai and Si side, so that three lines worked in step with the main force. Sun Hao was the protagonist of the losing side, and the tyranny and the endless levies of his reign were the root of the collapse in morale; he was made Marquis of Wucheng, taken to Luoyang, and died four years later.
kits: 卡面這件秦弩屬於弩機技術：弩把拉弦的力存進弩機，張弦以後可以久待，射時只須扣動機牙，射速遠勝拉弓，也不需要像弓手那樣常年拉臂。漢代以來弩就是軍隊中數量最多的遠射兵器，《後漢書·百官志》所記的虎賁營與步兵營都置有弩手；弩的形制有蹶張、腰張、擘張三種張法，機上有機牙、弦與望山，大型的用蹶張器或以足踏弓弦上弦。曹魏方面，傅玄《馬鈞傳》記馬鈞造「御弩」，可連發十矢，代表同時代弩的改進方向。本戰中弩正是決定水戰節奏的裝備：吳軍沿岸列弩手封鎖江面，晉軍舟師推進時必須以蒙衝硬撞吳舟，並以弩手在船頭掩護登岸之兵，吳岸的弩手與晉船的弩手隔江互射，射界之內誰先暴露誰就吃虧。除弩外，晉軍尚備環首刀、直刃劍、長矛長槊、戟與錘，著札甲、鎧甲、介冑兜鍪，配大盾、梟盾與虎頭牌；水戰用蒙衝、斗艦、樓船與走舸，攻城備雲梯、飛樓、撞車與投石車，後勤靠船隊兼作糧運。吳軍則以鐵鎖繫於江中、以竹篾編成浮橋橫截水道，這種攔阻器材與弩手配合，正是當年守江的老辦法。至於演義中常見的方天畫戟、青龍偃月刀、雌雄雙股劍，屬小說形制，史料並無記載，不應當作三國的制式裝備。
kitsEn: The Chinese crossbow on the card belongs to the technology of the trigger mechanism: the crossbow stores the force of the draw inside the lock, so the bow may be held cocked for a long time, and firing requires only the release of the trigger, which makes the rate of fire far higher than that of a bow and spares the archer the burden of keeping his arm drawn. From the Han dynasty onward the crossbow was the most numerous missile weapon in the army; the Baiguan Zhi of the Later Han records crossbowmen in both the Tiger Guard and the Infantry Guard, and the Han crossbow came in three ways of cocking, by foot, by waist and by the whole body, with a trigger, a string and a sight plate on the lock, the larger types cocked by a treadle or by the weight of the leg. On the Cao Wei side the biography of Ma Jun by Fu Xuan records that Ma Jun built an imperial crossbow able to loose ten bolts in succession, which shows the direction improvement had taken. In this war the crossbow was the equipment that set the rhythm of the fighting on the water. The Wu troops posted crossbowmen along the bank to seal the river, and the Jin flotilla had to force its way by ramming Wu vessels with mengchong, with crossbowmen ranged in the ship's bow to cover the soldiers who boarded the bank; the crossbowmen of the Wu shore and the crossbowmen of the Jin ships shot at one another across the water, and whoever was caught inside the beaten zone paid for it. Besides the crossbow, the Jin carried ring-pommel sabres, straight-edged swords, long spears and lances, halberds and maces, wore lamellar and plate armour with iron helmets and caps, and used large shields, wicker shields and tiger-headed boards. Their naval equipment was mengchong, doujian, tower ships and light runners; their siege train included scaling ladders, flying towers, battering rams and stone-throwers; and their logistics rode in the same fleet that carried the grain. The Wu, for their part, moored chains of iron in the river and wove screens of bamboo into a floating bridge that lay across the channel, and that obstacle, worked together with the crossbowmen on the bank, was the old method of holding a river. The fangtian huaji, the green dragon crescent blade and the twin-tined sword of the novel are fictional forms with no basis in the record and are not to be treated as standard equipment of the Three Kingdoms.
tactics: 晉軍的戰術是一場以舟師為主、陸路為輔的立體壓迫。第一步是分進合擊：六路大軍同時出動，王濬的舟師自成都沿長江東下，杜預自江陵、陶侃自武昌沿江推進，王渾與司馬伷分別自河南、淮泗南下，令吳軍無法判斷主攻方向，只能分兵處處設防。第二步是突破江防：吳人在板渚一線以竹篾、鐵鎖橫截江面，築浮橋拒敵，晉舟師受阻；杜預一面遣將攻擊吳將張悌所部，一面以小船載火炬、柴束夜渡江面，焚毀浮橋與繫舟，開出航道；此後晉舟師以蒙衝撞開吳軍舟陣，弩手在船前列陣，掩護士兵登岸奪取沿岸水寨。第三步是掃清江防：王濬的大船隊在三峽中順流疾下，出峽後連破吳軍水寨，經牛渚、三山直抵石頭城；陶侃一軍則在江陵與武昌之間逐次攻取吳軍沿岸營落，與舟師主力平行推進。第四步是受降：兵臨石頭城下，孫皓遣使乞降，晉軍入城收圖籍、押送吳官屬與孫皓北還，吳軍各部陸續放下兵器。整個過程的關鍵，是舟師的到達時間與弩的射程：只要吳岸弩手還能封住水面，晉軍就得逐點硬啃；一旦大船隊抵達石頭城下，吳廷便再無縱深可用。
tacticsEn: The Jin plan was a three-dimensional pressure with the fleet as its main body and the land routes in support. The first step was to advance separately and converge: all six columns moved at once, Wang Jun's fleet coming down the Yangtze from Chengdu, Du Yu and Tao Kan moving along the river from Jiangling and Wuchang, and Wang Hun and Sima Zhou coming south from Henan and from the Huai-Si basin, so that Wu could not tell which way the main blow would fall and had to spread its troops over every position. The second step was to break the river defence. At Ban Chu the Wu men laid bamboo screens and iron chains across the channel to form a floating bridge and hold the enemy off, and the Jin fleet was held up; Du Yu thereupon sent men to attack the troops of the Wu general Zhang Ti while at the same time putting torches and bundles of firewood into small boats, ferrying them across the river by night and burning the bridge and the moored craft, which opened a channel. From then on the Jin fleet rammed the Wu formations with mengchong, crossbowmen were ranged along the ship's bow, and the men who boarded the bank and took the riverside camps were covered as they landed. The third step was to sweep the river clear. Wang Jun's great ships came down through the Three Gorges and, once out of the narrows, broke camp after camp of the Wu fleet, passing Niuzhu and Sanshan and running straight to Stone City; Tao Kan's column in the meantime took the Wu shore camps one by one between Wuchang and Jiangling, moving level with the fleet. The last step was the surrender. With the army under the walls of Stone City, Sun Hao sent his envoys to beg for terms; the Jin entered the city, took the registers and records, and sent the Wu officials and Sun Hao north, while the Wu formations everywhere laid down their arms. The whole performance turned on the time of arrival of the fleet and on the reach of the crossbow: as long as the Wu bank could seal the water with its bolts, the Jin had to gnaw at the defences position by position, and once the great ships stood below Stone City, Wu had no depth left to fall back on.
data: 可核對的數字並不多，但足以看出規模。兵員方面，《晉書·武帝紀》記咸寧四年十一月詔令「率眾二十餘萬，自北南征」，是六路大軍的總數；史料未給出各路分兵數字，吳軍兵額與歷年大戰的實際投入亦無可靠記載，因此只能說兩岸各有數十萬量級的兵員被牽動，而吳軍分散在千餘里江防線上，調度遠不如晉軍集中。舟船方面，王濬所造連舫大船「方百二十步，受二千餘人」，一船即當一營兵力，蜀地工匠造這些船的同時還得供應糧秣。時間上，詔下於咸寧四年十一月，太康元年正月初戰，二月大軍抵達下游，三月王濬舟師直抵石頭、孫皓出降，全戰歷時約四個月，跨越一整個冬季。距離以今日里程計，自成都至建業順流約四千里，江陵至建業約三千里，武昌至建業約一千四百里，川江一段又加三峽之險，舟師必須同時解決上行的運力與下行的速度。射程上，弩的有效射程在百步上下，遠超弓的五十步左右；弩手可在城頭與船頭以近乎平射的姿勢持續覆蓋一段江面，這是雙方都敢在江上列陣的技術底氣。戰損方面，晉軍確切死傷數不見記載，只知板渚焚橋與衝撞之役吳軍死傷甚眾，吳廷的家底也在三年徵發與宮室工程中耗盡。
dataEn: The verifiable numbers are few but enough to show the scale. On men, the Emperor's Annals in the Book of Jin records that in the eleventh month of Xianning 4 the edict sent the columns out 'with more than two hundred thousand men, marching from the north to the south', which is the figure for the six columns together. The sources give no per-column breakdown, and there is no reliable record of the Wu order of battle or of what was actually committed in the fighting, so it can only be said that scores of thousands of men on both banks were drawn into the affair, while the Wu troops were scattered over a thousand li of river front and could not concentrate as the Jin did. On ships, Wang Jun's connected-deck vessel was 'a hundred and twenty paces across the beam, carrying more than two thousand men', so that a single hull was a battalion in transport, and while the craftsmen of Shu built them they also had to feed the army. On time, the edict came in the eleventh month of Xianning 4, the first fighting was in the first month of Taikang 1, the columns reached the lower river in the second month, and in the third month Wang Jun's fleet came to Stone City and Sun Hao surrendered; the whole campaign lasted about four months and straddled a full winter. On distance, measured in today's miles, the run from Chengdu to Jianye is roughly four thousand li down the water, Jiangling to Jianye about three thousand, and Wuchang to Jianye about one thousand four hundred, and the Sichuan reach adds the hazard of the Three Gorges, so the fleet had to solve at once the problem of carrying supplies upstream and of speed downstream. On range, the effective reach of the crossbow is on the order of a hundred paces, well beyond the bow's fifty, and a crossbowman could keep a stretch of river under a nearly flat trajectory from a wall head or a ship's bow; that is the technical confidence on which both sides were willing to line up on the water. On losses, no firm count of Jin dead and wounded survives, but the burning of the barrier at Ban Chu and the ramming that followed cost the Wu many men, and the resources of the Wu court had already been spent by three years of levies and palace building.
cause: 打起來的原因分三層。最外層是統一的邏輯：曹魏平定蜀漢之後，江北已歸於一統，剩下江南一隅的孫吳，於是成為任何一個北方政權都不能長期容忍的例外，滅吳是完成統一的最後一步。第二層是吳廷自身的崩壞：孫皓即位後誅戮臣下、逼遷宗室於吳郡、大興宮室土木、加派供役，士卒疲於轉輸，百姓怨怒；杜預所說的「國怨民疲」，正是當時吳地的實況，吳兵在江上不是不能打，而是不願為這樣的朝廷效死。第三層是晉方的長期準備與對吳的孤立：荊州方向的羊祜以屯田積穀、修農養兵、撫恤新附百姓，換來荊襄士民的歸心，杜預接任後主張乘勢而進；蜀漢降後益州已平，蜀中水軍與工匠可以直接投入東下之役；孫皓在內部清洗與外部進逼中逐漸失去人心，兩度遣使求和又屢屢遷延，等到晉軍兵臨城下，才在主降與主戰之間作了最後選擇。值得留意的是，朝議對此並非一致，認為可以緩兵相待、俟吳自敗者亦有人在，杜預上表力辯才促成出兵，於是這場戰爭並非全然必然，而是被一紙奏疏推到了必須立刻解決的地步。
causeEn: There were three layers behind the fighting. The outermost was the logic of unification: after Cao Wei had settled Shu, the north was already one realm, and the Jiangnan corner still held by Sun's Wu became an exception that no northern regime could tolerate for long, so the destruction of Wu was the last step towards completing the union. The second layer was the collapse of the Wu court itself. After taking the throne Sun Hao executed his ministers, pressed the imperial clan into Wu Commandery, built palaces without measure and added levies without end, so that the soldiers were worn out by transport and the people were full of anger; what Du Yu called 'the resentment of the country and the weariness of the people' was the actual state of Wu, and its soldiers on the river were not unable to fight but unwilling to die for such a court. The third layer was the long preparation on the Jin side and the isolation of Wu. In the Jingzhou direction Yang Hu had bought the hearts of the people of Jing and Xiang by ploughing and storing grain, resting the army and sparing the new subjects, and Du Yu, taking over from him, argued for pressing the advantage while it lasted. With Shu already settled, the river troops and craftsmen of Shu could be thrown into the eastern descent. And as Sun Hao purged his court and was pressed from without, he lost the hearts of his people, sent envoys to ask for terms twice and stalled both times, and only at the foot of the walls did he make his final choice between surrender and war. It should be noted that opinion at court was not unanimous, that there were men who held the army back and waited for Wu to ruin itself, and that Du Yu's memorial was what pushed the war to the point where it had to be settled at once.
impact: 吳亡之後，四百餘年的分裂局面第一次收束，中原重歸一統。這件事的後果卻極為反諷：太平只維持十來年，晉武帝一死，諸王爭權的內亂隨即爆發，八王之亂把中原折騰到崩潰，匈奴、鮮卑、羯、氐、羌等內遷勢力趁隙而起，永嘉之亂使北方陷於戰亂，衣冠南渡由此開端，江南第一次在制度與人口上成為中國的重心。吳國兩百餘年在江南留下的水利、屯田與開發成果則被西晉直接繼承，會稽、丹陽一帶的稻作、陂塘與航運在戰後仍照常運作，只是人口大量流失、廢田待墾，秩序待建。技術上，這場戰爭是弩在冷兵器時代的最後一次大規模水面演出：弩機的儲力結構讓攻防雙方都能以小量人力維持遠射壓制，也說明漢代確立的弩手編制在兩晉仍是軍隊骨幹；而曹魏馬鈞那具可連發十矢的御弩，若與三峽的舟師結合，本可改變攻防節奏，只是當時雙方都把它用在岸上而不是船上。文化上，陳壽《三國志》的吳書正是在此後不久寫定，裴松之為魏吳兩家的注補了大量逸聞，成為後世讀三國的基礎；至於演義所寫的「三國歸晉」一段，則是文學的收束，與史實的時間與細節並不重合。
impactEn: The fall of Wu closed, for the first time in more than four hundred years, a period of division and brought the country back under one rule. The consequence was bitterly ironic. The peace lasted barely a decade, and once Emperor Wu died the princes fell to fighting for the regency; the War of the Eight Princes tore the Central Plain apart, after which the Xiongnu, Xianbei, Jie, Di and Qiang pressed in from within, and the disaster of Yongjia plunged the north into war, sending the gentry of the central plains south. The great southward migration of the clans began there, and for the first time the Yangtze delta became the weighty centre of China in institutions and in people. The works of two centuries of Wu in the south, irrigation, reclamation and development, were inherited directly by Western Jin, and the rice cultivation, the embankment ponds and the river transport of Kuaiji and Danyang kept running after the war, though the population had been thinned by fighting and flight and the fields lay fallow waiting to be worked. In technical terms this war was the last great performance of the crossbow on a battlefield of the age: the locking mechanism let both sides sustain long-range pressure at small cost in manpower, and it showed that the crossbowman establishment settled in the Han was still the backbone of the armies of both Jin; the Wei repeating crossbow of Ma Jun, able to loose ten bolts in succession, could have changed the rhythm of attack and defence had it been put into boats rather than onto walls, but neither side did that. In cultural terms the Wu chapters of Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms were written down shortly afterwards, and Pei Songzhi's annotations to the records of Wei and Wu gathered a great deal of scattered material, becoming the base on which later generations read the Three Kingdoms. The novel's closing passage in which the Three Kingdoms return to Jin is, by contrast, a literary closure whose timing and detail do not match the record.
result: 打點完：太康元年三月，王濬的舟師抵達建業石頭城下，吳主孫皓率眾出降，東吳政權就此終結，歷時近六十年的三國並立局面以晉的統一收場。孫皓被封烏程侯，押送洛陽；吳官屬、將士先後北返，吳地的州郡改置刺史與將軍，宗室分封江淮以為屏藩，圖籍與府庫器物運往洛陽。晉廷對吳人的處置是募其北遷屯田，江南則因戰亂與逃亡而人口銳減，田地待墾，秩序待建。從兵器與戰術看，這場戰爭真正解決的問題是「江到底能不能渡得過去」：吳軍以弩與浮橋封江，晉軍以大船、蒙衝與夜焚浮橋破之，最後靠王濬舟師的直接抵達，而不是靠任何單一器械的先進取勝。史載孫皓出降時儀節屈辱，吳人相視而泣，陳壽在《三國志·吳主傳》亦以無幾語句記其末路。三國至此，弩手、環首刀與長槊所代表的三國軍隊形制，也隨著吳的覆亡退入史冊，成為後世兵家推演與摹擬的對象。
resultEn: The outcome was this: in the third month of Taikang 1 Wang Jun's fleet came to the foot of Stone City at Jianye, the Wu ruler Sun Hao came out and surrendered, and the state of Eastern Wu came to an end, closing the sixty-odd years of three concurrent realms with the union under Jin. Sun Hao was made Marquis of Wucheng and taken to Luoyang. The officials and soldiers of Wu were sent north in batches, the commanderies and counties of the former state were reorganised under inspectors and generals, the imperial clan was enfeoffed along the river as a screen, and the registers and the treasure of the Wu treasury were carried to Luoyang. The Jin court's handling of the Wu people was to recruit them north to settle and farm, while in the south the population had been thinned by the fighting and the flight, the fields waited to be worked and the order waited to be rebuilt. Seen from the point of view of weapons and tactics, the question this war actually settled was whether the river could be crossed at all: Wu sealed the water with crossbows and a floating barrier, and Jin broke that with great ships, mengchong and a barrier burned by night, winning in the end by the direct arrival of Wang Jun's fleet rather than by the superiority of any single instrument. The records describe Sun Hao's surrender as a humiliating business, with the people of Wu looking at one another and weeping, and Chen Shou's biography of the ruler of Wu in the Records of the Three Kingdoms dismisses his last days in a few lines. The Three Kingdoms ended, and the order of battle that the crossbowmen, the ring-pommel sabres and the long lances represented passed into the pages of history with the fall of Wu, to become a subject for later military writers to reconstruct and rehearse.
